OPENING SUMMARY — WEEK OF NOVEMBER 2 – 6, 2026

Week at a Glance:

A moderate week with one major release: EPA posted all five FY2027 Brownfields NOFOs on November 2 ($64,000,000 across Assessment, Coalition, State/Tribal, Revolving Loan Fund and Cleanup; all due January 21, 2027), the first cycle funded from annual appropriations alone, with the 20% cost share back for RLF and Cleanup and tighter caps. HUD opened two housing NOFOs ($98,000,000 Section 811 PRA for state housing agencies; $40,000,000 ROSS Service Coordinators), USDA APHIS released $80,000,000 in animal-disease preparedness agreements, DoD released the SERDP FY2028 solicitations (water, PFAS, critical-minerals refining), NASA opened EPSCoR ($21,000,000) and TEAM II, and NIH posted six institutional announcements. No new DOE, DOT (other than a niche NHTSA grant), FEMA, EDA, NOAA or DOL competitive NOFOs posted in the window; Congress was out for the November 3 midterms and the Federal Register was quiet on grant policy. California's notable item is the $55,000,000+ ZESBI school-bus round opening first-come on November 17; Michigan opened a $5,000,000 brownfield-solar round. Open Grant was unavailable this run (connector needs reconnecting), so the sweep relied on Grants.gov, agency sites, state portals and the Federal Register.

Brownfields (EPA FY2027):

EPA-OLEM-OBLR-26-02 through -26-06 — $64,000,000 total: Community-wide Assessment $15,000,000 (up to $500,000, ~30 awards), Assessment Coalition $13,000,000 (up to $1,000,000, cut from $1.5M), States and Tribes Assessment $12,000,000 (up to $1,000,000), Revolving Loan Fund $10,000,000 (up to $1,000,000, 20% cost share) and Cleanup $14,000,000 (up to $500,000, 20% cost share, applicant must own the site by the deadline). Local governments, COGs, states, tribes and 501(c)(3)s; no Multipurpose round this year. All due January 21, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET; webinars November 9 (Assessment) and November 12 (RLF/Cleanup); Cleanup applicants must publish a community notice by January 7 and hold a public meeting by January 14, 2027 or be disqualified.

Housing and Community Development:

HUD Section 811 Project Rental Assistance FY2027 (HSG-2700-DC-0053) — $98,000,000, up to $7,094,211, ~14 awards; state housing agencies only, with a signed partnership agreement with the state Medicaid and HHS agencies; due April 20, 2027. HUD ROSS Service Coordinator FY2026 (PIH-2600-DC-0005) — ~$40,000,000, $272,250–$816,750 by unit count, ~143 awards; PHAs, tribes/TDHEs, resident associations and PHA-backed nonprofits; 25% match (non-curable); due January 5, 2027. Michigan EGLE opened the $5,000,000 MI Brightfields Round 1 for solar and storage on contaminated sites (up to $2,000,000; local governments and tribes; due December 13, 2026).

Agriculture — Animal Disease Preparedness:

USDA APHIS NADPRP FY2027 — two NOFOs, each up to $40,000,000: State Preparedness (USDA-APHIS-10025-VSSP0000-27-0002; $500,000–$2,000,000, ~40 awards; state agriculture departments, state animal health officials and four regional alliances only) and Industry Preparedness (-27-0001; $500,000–$4,000,000, 15–20 awards; producer and veterinary organizations only). Universities, tribes and state labs participate as subawardees. Due January 7, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET via ezFedGrants (not Grants.gov). FDA also posted its three recurring state food-safety cooperative agreement PARs ($56,500,000 combined; state and territorial food regulatory agencies only; LOIs December 4–18, applications January 4–19, 2027).

Hazard Science and Natural Resources Research:

USGS Cooperative Landslide Hazard Mapping FY2027 (G27AS00381) — $1,000,000, $10,000–$150,000, ~10 awards; state, tribal, territorial and local governments (universities only on behalf of a state survey); no match; listing says February 1, 2027 but the NOFO says January 29, 2027, 5:00 p.m. ET — plan for January 29. USGS also posted about 26 Cooperative Ecosystem Studies Unit agreements ($200,000–$480,000 each; CESU member institutions only; most close November 30–December 7, 2026).

Transportation Safety:

NHTSA State Process for Informing Consumers of Recalls (NHTSA-693JJ927R000007-FY27) — up to $1,500,000; 3–5 awards of about $300,000–$500,000; state motor vehicle registration agencies only, one per state, prior awardees (Maryland) ineligible; no match; questions December 1; due February 4, 2027, 5:00 p.m. ET. Last year NHTSA can obligate under this authority.

Justice and Public Safety:

BJA FY26 SCAAP (O-BJA-2026-172810) — up to $177,684,621 in formula reimbursements to states, counties and cities that incarcerated undocumented criminal aliens July 2024–June 2025; three certifications including 8 U.S.C. § 1373 compliance; SAM.gov registration must begin by November 12; Grants.gov December 15, JustGrants December 22, 2026. BJA Special Attorneys Program Round 11 (O-BJA-2026-172812) — $300,000,000 program-wide, 100% prosecutor salary and fringe plus 20% for capacity; state, local and tribal governments employing prosecutors, with an immigration-cooperation certification; Grants.gov November 17, 2026, JustGrants November 19. SAMHSA forecast the First Responders–CARA cooperative agreements (TI-27-006; ~$20,000,000, 40 awards; NOFO expected December 15).

Education, Research and Culture:

NASA EPSCoR FY2027 Basic Research (NNH27ZHA001C) — $21,000,000, up to $750,000, 28 awards; institutions in EPSCoR jurisdictions via the state NASA EPSCoR Director; cost share required (percentage not on the listing); due February 1, 2027. NASA TEAM II STEM Innovator (NNH27ZHA002C) — $4,000,000, up to $250,000, 16 awards; nonprofit informal-education institutions lead; due February 1, 2027. NEH Endowments for Advancing the Humanities (20270113-CHE) — $10,000,000, $1,000,000–$3,100,000, 5 awards, 1:1 nonfederal match; colleges, universities, local and tribal governments and 501(c)(3)s; due January 13, 2027. DoD SERDP FY2028 Core and SEED solicitations (stormwater, PFAS residuals, water resilience, critical-minerals refining, coatings; webinar November 20; Core pre-proposals January 7, 2027). NIH posted six institutional announcements: RFA-AI-28-014 systems biology of infection ($26,000,000, Feb 18), NIDDK DGIC centers RFA-DK-28-213/-214 (Feb 5 new), O'Brien Urology Centers RFA-DK-28-314 (Feb 1), suicide-prevention provider training RFA-MH-28-145 (Feb 17), ADRD genomic therapies RFA-NS-28-012 (Feb 9) and cancer assay validation PAR-28-042 (Feb 16).

California:

CEC/CARB Zero-Emission School Bus and Infrastructure (ZESBI) second solicitation — at least $55,000,000, first-come within three priority tiers; California LEAs only; application acceptance opens November 17, 2026, 10:00 a.m. PT (pre-application uploads open now; readiness on day one decides the outcome). CDFA 2027 CNIP Expansion — $750,000, $10,000–$300,000, nonprofit farmers' market operators, due December 4, 2026. Cal OES Human Trafficking Vertical Prosecution — $9,000,000, district attorneys' offices only, due January 8, 2027.

Human Services — Volunteer Caregiver Support:

ACL-funded Community Care Corps, Cohort 7 (2027–2028) — about $3,570,000 in Oasis Institute subawards ($1,500,000 reserved for volunteer chaperone transportation to medical appointments); 18-month grants of $30,000–$200,000; nonprofit lead applicant required (Area Agencies on Aging, tribal entities, faith-based groups, local governments, health systems and universities as applicants or partners); 25% match (cash or in-kind); due January 6, 2027, 5:00 p.m. ET. Added from the newsletter Kristin forwarded; the RFP has been open since October 19 and ACL announced it November 2.

Policy & Compliance Updates:

PHMSA proposed the first comprehensive rewrite of the LNG facility safety rules since 2006 (91 FR 69314; comments January 4, 2027; small-scale and peak-shaving utilities affected). The Department of Education proposed amending its discretionary-grant Supplemental Priorities to add Registered Apprenticeship, tribal and "Super Intelligence" provisions (91 FR 69736; comments December 7). Treasury and IRS designated 6,576 Qualified Opportunity Zone tracts effective January 1, 2027. HHS finalized the Section 504 gender-dysphoria exclusion for all HHS grantees (91 FR 69207; effective January 4, 2027). NRC finalized streamlined contested licensing hearings (91 FR 69446; effective December 3). USDA Rural Development is building a single online loan and grant application platform (91 FR 69525; comments December 4); HUD is standing up HUGS portal financial documentation for all grantees (comments November 30) and waived the 30-day period for the FY2026 CoC NOFO (awards by December 1). The Section 232 robotics proclamation covered last week is now Proclamation 11077, 91 FR 69199 (no tariff; 180-day report). No 2 CFR 200 changes, BABA actions, grant-condition certifications or energy tax-credit guidance issued this week.

Watch List / Upcoming:

CEC GFO-25-603 NEVI Solicitation 6 Community Charging (up to $79,000,000): CEC issued the Questions and Answers Round 2 document on November 6 (GovDelivery notice forwarded by Kristin); the solicitation page as fetched still listed only Round 1 and Addenda 1–5, so pull Round 2 from the page before finalizing — applications due November 20, 2026, 11:59 p.m. via ECAMS. Near-term dates from items already covered: Grid SCALED concept papers November 20 (no amendment or FAQ posted; eXCHANGE still does not render); DoD SBIR/STTR FY27 Release 1 closes November 25 and Release 2 pre-released November 3 (opens December 2, closes January 6, 2027, 12:00 p.m. ET); PROSPECT Implementation Prize November 25; DOE SBIR Fall 2026 pitches December 16; AFOSR–Taiwan pre-proposals November 18; NSF 27-011 November 10; NOAA CPO LOI November 17; tribal BABA waiver comments November 23; MLRP comments December 7; HOMES RFP-26-501 pre-bid November 10; GFO-26-503 DEBA questions November 13. CDFW's Delta golden mussel call added a workshop (November 18, 10:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m. PST; concepts due December 15); the Call for Concepts PDF is still not posted, so eligibility and award terms remain unverified. Boating Access FY2027/28 closed November 5. DOE AFFO NOFO DE-FOA-0003649 still not posted (only the October 13 NOI; AFFO is recruiting ASPECT reviewers by November 18). DOT BUILD FY2027 not posted (FY2026 NOFO came mid-December); PIDP, CRISI, SS4A and Low-No FY27 rounds depend on FY2027 appropriations. DARPA: Laguna special notice DARPA-SN-27-15 (bio-based specialty chemicals) responses November 30; Cattle Run Proposers Day November 10; ONR FY27 MURI white papers November 20, 5:00 p.m. ET. ESTCP FY2028 expected (SERDP out November 5). Forecasts: SAMHSA FR-CARA NOFO ~December 15; HUD ICDBG NOFO December 16 (due March 31, 2027); HRSA-27-109 Rural Health IT Assessment (post March 29, 2027); NIH RFA-DK-28-113 (post December 1, due February 10, 2027). California: CORE FY2026-27 opens December 1, 9:00 a.m. PT; State Water Board adopted Prop 4 Stormwater Grant Program guidelines October 6 ($110,000,000; solicitation timing TBD); DWR Dam Safety PSP still pending; CTC LPP/SCCP/TCEP due November 18–20; EDD ETPP November 9; CalVCB TRC December 15. Other states: NYSERDA PON 6149 Grid Enhancing Technologies ($24,000,000, 50% cost share, rolling to 2029); MassCEC workforce training rounds November 23; TCEQ GAFF opening December; THIVE still unverifiable at a Texas agency source. Other: USGS landslide listing/NOFO deadline conflict (Feb 1 vs Jan 29); USDA announced an additional $50,000,000 in non-competitive NSLP equipment funds (unclear whether it flows through the posted Harvest to Hallways listing); HUD 811 PRA NOFO PDF not yet attached; NASA ROSES-2025 added D.10 Astrophysics Theory (NNH25ZDA001N-ATP, due February 3, 2027). grants.Description: EPA — FY27 Brownfield Assessment Grants: Community-wide Assessment
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. EPA, Office of Land and Emergency Management, Office of Brownfields and Land Revitalization (Assistance Listing 66.818). HQ contact Elyse Salinas, brownfields@epa.gov; eligibility questions go to Regional Brownfields Contacts — Region 9 (AZ, CA, HI, NV, Pacific Islands) Jennifer Tung, Tung.Jennifer@epa.gov, (415) 972-3698; Region 6 (TX, NM, OK, AR, LA) Mike Kennedy, Kennedy.Michael@epa.gov, (214) 665-7125; Region 10 Meredith Lightbody, Lightbody.Meredith@epa.gov, (206) 553-6910.
grants.Total Funding: $15,000,000 (subject to appropriations). FY2027 grants are funded from annual appropriations only; the IIJA Brownfields money is spent, so the FY27 pool is smaller than FY24–FY26 and there is no Multipurpose competition in FY27.
grants.Award Range: Up to $500,000 per award; approximately 30 awards. Site-specific activities capped at $200,000 per site (EPA may waive up to $350,000); 4-year project period.
grants.Eligible Applicants: General-purpose local governments (counties, municipalities, towns, school districts); land clearance authorities and quasi-governmental entities under local control; regional councils and groups of local governments; state-chartered redevelopment agencies; states and territories; federally recognized tribes (other than Alaska, except Metlakatla) and intertribal consortia; Alaska Native Regional and Village Corporations; 501(c)(3) nonprofits including nonprofit colleges and universities; LLCs/LPs controlled by 501(c)(3)s; qualified community development entities. Excluded: individuals, for-profits, non-501(c)(3) nonprofits. One application per applicant. Threshold: current Assessment/Multipurpose recipients must have drawn down and disbursed at least 70.00% of each open agreement by October 1, 2026; holders of an open States-and-Tribes (CWAGST) grant are ineligible. New post-selection SAM.gov exclusion and risk review. No letter of intent.
grants.Deadline: January 21, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET via Grants.gov (the listing shows no time; the NOFO specifies 11:59 p.m. ET). National outreach webinar November 9, 2026, 1:00 p.m. ET (Zoom usepa.zoomgov.com/j/1657592522). Selections expected June 2027; awards September 2027.
grants.Program Focus: Funds brownfield inventories, Phase I/II environmental site assessments, cleanup planning, community involvement and area-wide reuse planning across a community; no cleanup work. What changed for FY27 (EPA's summary of guideline changes): the $200,000-per-site cap returns after being waived in FY26; the past-performance window narrows to grants closed 2016 or later; the "economically impoverished/disproportionately impacted" criterion is replaced by a disaster-preparedness and resilience criterion; and a new Other Factor favors applicants with no federal assistance agreements (or none since 2016). Other Factors also credit populations of 15,000 or less, tribes and territories, mine-scarred land, waterfront and floodplain sites, renewable-energy or energy-efficiency reuse, extreme-weather resilience, and target areas hit by a coal-plant closure since 2016. Review criteria total 155 points; narrative capped at 10 single-spaced pages plus a 3-page Application Information Sheet. Action: this is GMA's strongest broad-market item of the week — a campaign to cities, counties, COGs, tribes and redevelopment agencies with industrial or energy-community legacy sites, aimed first at jurisdictions that have never held an EPA Brownfields grant (the new first-time factor and smaller ceilings make small jurisdictions more competitive). Register clients for the November 9 webinar and confirm the 70% drawdown threshold for any current grantee before scoping.
grants.Cost Share / Match: None; voluntary cost share will not be accepted.

grants.Description: EPA — FY27 Brownfield Assessment Grants: Assessment Coalition
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. EPA, Office of Land and Emergency Management, Office of Brownfields and Land Revitalization (Assistance Listing 66.818). HQ contact Elyse Salinas, brownfields@epa.gov; eligibility questions go to Regional Brownfields Contacts — Region 9 (AZ, CA, HI, NV, Pacific Islands) Jennifer Tung, Tung.Jennifer@epa.gov, (415) 972-3698; Region 6 (TX, NM, OK, AR, LA) Mike Kennedy, Kennedy.Michael@epa.gov, (214) 665-7125; Region 10 Meredith Lightbody, Lightbody.Meredith@epa.gov, (206) 553-6910.
grants.Award Range: Up to $1,000,000 per coalition (reduced from $1,500,000 in FY26); approximately 13 awards. $200,000-per-site cap (waiver to $350,000); 4-year project period.
grants.Eligible Applicants: Same entity types as the Community-wide grant. Structure: one lead plus two to four non-lead members, all separate legal entities, fixed at the deadline; target areas must not overlap and must span at least three jurisdictions; each member must have at least two sites assessed in its boundary; MOA before any drawdown. New threshold: at least one non-lead member must never have received an EPA MARC grant (or its last one closed 2015 or earlier). The 70.00% drawdown-by-October 1, 2026 rule now applies to lead and non-lead members; open CWAGST holders cannot be lead or member; one Coalition application per applicant.
grants.Deadline: January 21, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET via Grants.gov. National outreach webinar November 9, 2026, 1:00 p.m. ET (Zoom usepa.zoomgov.com/j/1657592522). Selections June 2027; awards September 2027.
grants.Program Focus: Multi-jurisdiction assessment and planning programs led by a county, COG, state agency, tribe or 501(c)(3) with small-town or rural partners. The FY27 changes cut the ceiling by a third and force the inclusion of a never-funded member, which rewards regional councils that can recruit small jurisdictions quickly. Review criteria total 160 points; 12-page narrative. Action: pitch to COGs, regional planning commissions, county economic development agencies and tribal consortia; the member-recruitment rule is the first task and the long pole, so coalition formation should start in November.
grants.Cost Share / Match: None; voluntary cost share not accepted.

grants.Description: EPA — FY27 Brownfield Assessment Grants: Community-wide Assessment for States and Tribes (CWAGST)
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. EPA, Office of Land and Emergency Management, Office of Brownfields and Land Revitalization (Assistance Listing 66.818). HQ contact Elyse Salinas, brownfields@epa.gov; eligibility questions go to Regional Brownfields Contacts — Region 9 (AZ, CA, HI, NV, Pacific Islands) Jennifer Tung, Tung.Jennifer@epa.gov, (415) 972-3698; Region 6 (TX, NM, OK, AR, LA) Mike Kennedy, Kennedy.Michael@epa.gov, (214) 665-7125; Region 10 Meredith Lightbody, Lightbody.Meredith@epa.gov, (206) 553-6910.
grants.Award Range: Up to $1,000,000; approximately 12 awards; 5-year project period. Must assess at least 10 sites across the applicant's geography, with at least three target areas and five priority sites.
grants.Eligible Applicants: States (agencies under the governor's direct control — environmental, transportation, health, parks, commerce departments) and federally recognized tribes/intertribal consortia only; Alaska Native Regional and Village Corporations and Metlakatla. State and tribal universities are not eligible for this type. One application per state agency and per tribal nation (agencies under the same executive count as one). Current CWAGST recipients must show at least 60.00% disbursed by October 1, 2026. A CWAGST applicant may not also apply for an FY27 Community-wide or Coalition grant or join a coalition.
grants.Deadline: January 21, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET via Grants.gov. National outreach webinar November 9, 2026, 1:00 p.m. ET (Zoom usepa.zoomgov.com/j/1657592522).
grants.Program Focus: Statewide or tribe-wide assessment programs — for example a state DOT or commerce department assessing corridor or industrial-reuse sites, or a tribe assessing former industrial, mining or fuel-storage parcels across its lands. 155 points; 12-page narrative. Action: a direct pitch to state agency and tribal government clients; because the three Assessment types are mutually exclusive, help each client choose the right vehicle before anyone starts writing.

grants.Description: EPA — FY27 Brownfield Revolving Loan Fund (RLF) Grants
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. EPA, Office of Land and Emergency Management, Office of Brownfields and Land Revitalization (Assistance Listing 66.818). HQ contact Elyse Salinas, brownfields@epa.gov; eligibility questions go to Regional Brownfields Contacts — Region 9 (AZ, CA, HI, NV, Pacific Islands) Jennifer Tung, Tung.Jennifer@epa.gov, (415) 972-3698; Region 6 (TX, NM, OK, AR, LA) Mike Kennedy, Kennedy.Michael@epa.gov, (214) 665-7125; Region 10 Meredith Lightbody, Lightbody.Meredith@epa.gov, (206) 553-6910. RLF/Cleanup Region 9 contact Daniel Moher, moher.daniel@epa.gov, (415) 972-3210.
grants.Award Range: Up to $1,000,000 of EPA funds; approximately 10 awards; 5-year project period. At least 50% of the total award (EPA funds plus cost share) must go to loans and loan-program costs; the remainder may be subgrants.
grants.Eligible Applicants: Same governmental, tribal and 501(c)(3) entity types as the Assessment grants (individuals, for-profits and non-501(c)(3) nonprofits ineligible). Any entity with an open Brownfields RLF cooperative agreement, or that is a non-lead member of one, is ineligible. RLF coalitions allowed (members fixed at the deadline). Thresholds: defined RLF geographic boundary; cleanup-oversight approach plus a legal opinion on authority to run a loan/subgrant program; contractor and subrecipient disclosure; cost-share plan. An entity cannot apply for both an FY27 RLF and an FY27 Cleanup grant.
grants.Deadline: January 21, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET via Grants.gov. National outreach webinar November 12, 2026, 2:00 p.m. ET (Zoom usepa.zoomgov.com/j/1652924178).
grants.Program Focus: Capitalizes a locally run revolving loan fund (loans and subgrants) for brownfield cleanups. First RLF competition since FY25 (none in FY26) and the first in years with the CERCLA 20% cost share back in force. Point total is now 185 with weight shifted to task/cost and programmatic capability; a new Other Factor favors jurisdictions with no access to any open RLF. 12-page narrative. Action: fits counties, cities, regional development authorities, port authorities and tribes that want a reusable cleanup-financing tool; stacks with Cleanup grants held by subrecipients and with state brownfield programs. Confirm the client's legal authority to lend before committing.
grants.Cost Share / Match: 20% of federal funds (e.g., $200,000 on a $1,000,000 award) in cash, labor, materials or services; territories exempt; hardship waiver for governments of 50,000 or fewer, tribes and nonprofits via a 2-page Hardship Waiver Request submitted with the application — EPA says approvals will be "extremely limited." The Grants.gov field says "cost sharing: No" but the NOFO requires 20% — the NOFO governs.

grants.Award Range: Up to $500,000 per application (one site or several); approximately 28 awards; 4-year project period. grants.Eligible Applicants: Same entity types as the Assessment grants plus other nonprofits and nonprofit colleges and universities; individuals and for-profits excluded. Thresholds: applicant must be the sole owner of each site (fee simple or EPA-approved equivalent) by January 21, 2027, with deed or ownership documentation attached; a Phase II ESA (ASTM E1903-19 or equivalent; draft acceptable) completed before submission; a draft Analysis of Brownfield Cleanup Alternatives per site; a current FY27 state or tribal acknowledgement letter (prior-year letters not accepted); community notification ad published by January 7, 2027 and public meeting held by January 14, 2027 — failure disqualifies; no prior Cleanup grant for the site; site not on the NPL; one Cleanup application per applicant; cannot also apply for FY27 RLF; Multipurpose holders must meet the 70% drawdown rule.
grants.Deadline: January 21, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET via Grants.gov. National outreach webinar November 12, 2026, 2:00 p.m. ET (Zoom usepa.zoomgov.com/j/1652924178). Internal milestones: notice ad by January 7, public meeting by January 14, 2027.
grants.Program Focus: Direct cleanup of hazardous-substance and petroleum contamination at applicant-owned sites. Compared with FY26 the ceiling drops to $500,000, the 20% cost share returns, and the community-notification calendar moves earlier (ad at least 7 days before the meeting, meeting at least 7 days before the deadline). 175 points; 10-page narrative. Action: strongest for municipalities, port and redevelopment authorities, tribes and nonprofits that already own an assessed site and can line up a 20% match or a credible hardship case. For a late-starting client the January 7/14 notification deadlines, the ownership-by-deadline rule and the Phase II requirement are the binding constraints — screen for site ownership and an existing Phase II first.
grants.Cost Share / Match: 20% of federal funds ($100,000 on a $500,000 award), cash or in-kind for eligible costs incurred after selection; territories exempt; hardship waiver (governments of 50,000 or fewer, tribes, nonprofits) via a 2-page request with unemployment, income, out-migration, disaster and fiscal-capacity data; decision announced with selections. Voluntary cost share above 20% not accepted.

grants.Description: HUD — Section 811 Project Rental Assistance (PRA) Program FY2027
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, Office of Housing (Multifamily). Contact Marketta Morris, 811PRANOFO@HUD.GOV (no phone listed).
grants.Award Range: $1 floor (placeholder) – $7,094,211 ceiling; 14 expected awards.
grants.Eligible Applicants: State (or local) housing agencies that allocate Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or administer HOME or similar programs only. Hard requirement: a signed Inter-Agency Partnership Agreement with the state Health and Human Services agency and the state Medicaid agency. Only one applicant per state can be funded; if several apply, the Medicaid/HHS agency chooses the partner, and if that agency appears on multiple applications none is considered. Individuals, foreign entities and sole proprietorships ineligible.
grants.Deadline: April 20, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET via Grants.gov. No letter of intent.
grants.Program Focus: Funds state-level project rental assistance contracts that place supportive housing units for extremely low-income people with disabilities inside existing or new affordable multifamily properties (LIHTC and HOME pipelines), with services coordinated through the state Medicaid/HHS partnership. The housing agency may administer PRA contracts directly or through qualified sub-contracted entities. The 5.5-month runway favors states that still need to negotiate the inter-agency agreement. Action: outreach to state housing finance agency clients and to Medicaid/HHS agencies that must co-sign; LIHTC developer clients should know which states will compete so they can plan PRA-covered units in 2027 applications. grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
grants.Summary: HUD seeks OMB approval for a new collection of financial documentation that grant recipients will upload through the HUD Grants System (HUGS) Recipient Portal, and renewal of post-award reporting for Community Compass technical assistance awards. The HUGS notice confirms HUD's new grants system will require recipient financial-documentation uploads.
grants.Who It Affects: All HUD discretionary grantees migrating to HUGS (PHAs, tribes/TDHEs, CoC recipients, local governments, nonprofits); technical-assistance providers.
grants.GMA Action Items: Comment by November 30 if portal documentation burden is a concern; brief HUD grantee clients on HUGS financial-documentation requirements ahead of the FY2026–FY2027 award cycle.

grants.Description: HUD — Waiver of the 30-Day Application Period for the FY2026 Continuum of Care Program NOFO
grants.Issuing Agency: HUD, Office of the Deputy Secretary
grants.Effective Date: Waiver already executed; statutory award deadline December 1, 2026.
grants.Summary: HUD formally waived the HUD Reform Act § 102(a) 30-day minimum application period for the FY2026 CoC NOFO. Per the notice: NOFO published June 1, 2026 (August 26 deadline); modified July 24 to add a direct-to-HUD route for areas without a collaborative applicant; vacated by the District of Rhode Island August 7; stayed by the First Circuit September 16; reopened September 18 with a 12-day window closing September 30. HUD counts about 80 cumulative days, nearly 8,000 project applications (about 3,500 new) and almost 400 CoC applications, with Congress requiring awards by December 1.
grants.Who It Affects: CoC collaborative applicants, homeless-services nonprofits, PHAs and local governments awaiting FY2026 CoC awards.
grants.GMA Action Items: Tell CoC clients to expect award notices by December 1 and prepare for compressed post-award timelines; monitor the First Circuit appeal for further disruption.

grants.Description: Treasury CDFI Fund — Revised CDFI/NACA Financial and Technical Assistance Applications, NMTC CDE Certification and Performance Reporting Forms (Information Collections)
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Community Development Financial Institutions Fund
grants.Summary: The CDFI Fund is revising the CDFI Program and Native American CDFI Assistance (NACA) FA/TA applications, adding optional questions on Persistent Poverty Counties, Disability Funds and the Healthy Food Financing Initiative and stating that changes were made to align with executive orders and reduce waste, fraud and abuse. Separately it seeks comment on the NMTC Community Development Entity certification application and the AMIS-based Performance Progress Report and Financial Statement Audit Report forms.
grants.Who It Affects: CDFIs, Native CDFIs, NMTC community development entities and their nonprofit and municipal partners; indirectly, community-facility and small-business borrowers.
grants.GMA Action Items: Review the revised FA/TA application for new certification or EO-alignment questions; comment by December 29 if the changes raise eligibility or burden concerns for CDFI clients.

grants.Description: USDA NIFA — SBIR/STTR "Lifecycle Certification" Form (New Information Collection); plus FAA PFC and MARAD Deepwater Port Proposed Rules
grants.Reference #: 91 FR 69789; FR Doc. 2026-22616; OMB 0524-0053. Also: FAA Passenger Facility Charge SNPRM, 91 FR 69511, FR Doc. 2026-22450 (comments January 4, 2027); MARAD Deepwater Port Application Processing NPRM, 91 FR 69768, FR Doc. 2026-22617 (comments January 4, 2027)
grants.Issuing Agency: USDA National Institute of Food and Agriculture; DOT FAA; DOT MARAD
grants.Effective Date: NIFA comments due December 7, 2026; FAA and MARAD comments due January 4, 2027.
grants.Summary: NIFA would require USDA SBIR/STTR Phase I and II awardees to submit a Lifecycle Certification with interim and final reports confirming continued small-business eligibility, per SBA policy. The FAA supplemental proposal implements the 2024 Reauthorization Act's PFC changes (reduced turnback, two new eligible project types, review timelines for notices of intent, streamlined review). MARAD's proposal implements the FY2026 NDAA transfer of deepwater-port license processing from the Coast Guard to MARAD as NEPA lead.
grants.Who It Affects: Agricultural and rural-tech small businesses with USDA SBIR/STTR awards; airport sponsors using PFC revenue as local match for AIP/BIL grants; port authorities and offshore energy/LNG developers.
grants.GMA Action Items: Add the lifecycle certification to SBIR compliance checklists for USDA awardees; share the PFC and deepwater-port proposals with airport and port clients and comment where capital plans are affected.
